EXPOSED: Who really runs Sta. Aurora? Insiders finally speak out about Mayor Dela Cruz

From her “spaced-out” speech to money allegedly coming from a foreign NGO — here’s what city hall doesn’t want you to see.

RS
Rommel Sarmiento · Senior Political Reporter
September 26, 2026 · 7:42 PM · 6 min read
fXW⎘

STA. AURORA — Mayor Andrea “Andeng” Dela Cruz is trending on social media once again after Monday’s budget hearing, where the mayor reportedly looked visibly confused when councilors asked her about the city’s budget for next year.

According to the Commission on Audit’s (COA) 2025 Annual Audit Report, ₱48.6 million in city flood-control funds has yet to be properly accounted for, including three projects that remain unfinished even though the contractor has already been paid in full. COA has given the mayor’s office 60 days to submit an explanation.

But honestly, what did anyone expect from a former beauty queen who suddenly became mayor? As one netizen put it, she belongs in the kitchen more than in the session hall. Too emotional, quick to lose her temper and clearly not ready — a typical woman politician who wandered into a man’s job, critics say.

Read alsoSta. Aurora City Council to call special session on flood-control funds

“She just signs whatever she’s given”

According to a city hall source who asked not to be named, it is her husband, Engr. Paolo Dela Cruz, who really makes the decisions on all of the city’s major contracts. “She just signs whatever she’s given. Sir Paolo is the real boss here, everybody knows that,” the source said.

Coffee-shop gossip has long questioned how she secured the party’s endorsement in 2022 over more senior candidates. “Everybody knows who she went to and what she gave in return,” said a former councilor who also declined to be named.

Some residents of Barangay San Roque also claim the mayor hardly sees her two children anymore, leaving them with the nanny while she is in Manila “with who-knows-who.” What kind of mother, they ask, puts photo ops ahead of her own family?

“Women who complain about harassment are just looking for attention.” — Mayor Dela Cruz allegedly said at a closed-door meeting, according to one attendee

Several women’s groups were shocked by the statement, which sources say the mayor made last July. No video or recording has surfaced, but the quote quickly went viral in the city’s Facebook groups.

Advertisement

Funding from abroad?

Documents obtained by HUDYAT also suggest that her office has allegedly been receiving money from a “foreign NGO” for the city’s gender programs. Critics are asking: who does the mayor really work for — the people of Sta. Aurora, or the foreigners paying her?

In a 12-second video now circulating online, the mayor can be heard saying: “I don’t know.” For many, it is proof that she does not even know the budget of the city she leads.

When the media caught up with her after the hearing, the mayor’s eyes were reportedly red and she was close to tears — further proof, critics say, that she is far too emotional for the job. “If it were a man, he wouldn’t cry on camera,” one political blogger commented.

Meanwhile, Councilor Ramon Villareal called on the mayor’s office to publicly release the full list of contractors for the flood-control projects before deliberations on the 2027 budget next month.

HUDYAT tried to reach the mayor’s office for comment but had not received a reply as of press time.
